ai_show_review.summary: Monster Viola Lee Blues, soaring Clementine and tight Other One suite
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a blistering Viola Lee Blues and a luminous Clementine, with the Other One suite flowing through Cryptical Envelopments. Jerry's guitar soars while Phil lays down a solid bass foundation. The high‑energy set is captured on three soundboard sources.
ai_show_review.review: The Crystal Ballroom show of February 2, 1968 captures the Dead in an early‑68 blaze of creativity. From the opening roar of Viola Lee Blues—where Garcia’s wailing lead guitar rides atop a thunderous rhythm—to the seamless Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment sequence, the band moves with tight, jazz‑inflected confidence. Clementine shines as a soaring, melodic centerpiece, and even the brief Good Morning Little School Girl keeps the momentum alive despite a minor early cut in one source. Across all three soundboard recordings the energy stays high, but the Jools‑Jools capture (gd68-02-02.sbd.jools.15801.sbeok.shnf) remains the most complete, preserving every song and transition while still delivering a clear, listenable mix.

best_recording.reason: Most complete capture of the set with all six songs intact; despite slight muddiness it retains clear guitar and vocal presence.

key_highlights: Monster Viola Lee Blues with blistering Garcia leads
Luminous Clementine that showcases tight band interplay
The Other One suite flowing through Cryptical Envelopments
High‑energy performance captured across three soundboard sources

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as wailing, soaring and perfect in tone, especially on Viola Lee Blues and throughout Clementine.
band_performance.Phil: Phil provides a solid, powerful bass foundation, "bombing" during Clementine and anchoring the extended jams.
